data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the subject's observable behavior is causally downstream of the test's own guard; the 1/9 vs 4/4 to 6/7 distribution shows that compile.py was the only module where the test's guard did not already exist in the acceptance record, so the one mutation lost under shown-to-fail-first installation was the only one that could have been constrained but was instead masked.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If compile.py had an ordinarily-guarded test path like the other modules, the 1/9 loss would disappear.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the other modules' guards were removed and their mutations still failed, the distribution would be uniform.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the acceptance record's guard coverage were audited and shown to be uniform across modules, the confound would be ruled out.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The guard in compile.py was not part of the acceptance record's ordinary path, so when the mutation was shown to fail first, the guard's absence meant the test could not distinguish the mutation from the failure. In every other module, the guard was already present, so the test constrained the mutation by requiring the guard to hold.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
